headline: 273 METRES AT 1.1 g/t: Sitka Gold Drills to Record 1,093m Depth at Yukon's Blackjack Zone
snippet: Sitka Gold's deepest-ever hole at its RC Gold project in Yukon returned 273.8m at 1.1 g/t gold from 1,093m depth — including 71.3m at 2.15 g/t and 10.4m at 7.39 g/t — confirming that the high-grade Blackjack zone extends well below the current open-pit resource model and opening a credible underground scenario.

headline: PROSPECTOR METALS TURNS DRILL IN YUKON: Fully Funded 25,000m Campaign Opens at ML Gold-Silver-Copper Target
snippet: Prospector Metals Corp. has commenced a fully funded 25,000-metre drill program at its ML gold-silver-copper project in Yukon, opening with step-out drilling at the high-grade TESS Zone discovery before testing a broader pipeline of district targets. The company plans to test the full strike and depth extent of the system this summer season.

headline: 17.88 g/t OVER 11m INCLUDING 42.53 g/t OVER 4.5m: Trident Resources Delivers Strongest-Ever Hit at Contact Lake
snippet: Trident Resources intersected 17.88 g/t Au over 11.25m including 42.53 g/t over 4.50m from just 86m depth at the Contact Lake Gold Project in northern Saskatchewan. The result tops the company's previous best hole — a 51.83m at 15.11 g/t from the BK3 Zone — and supports a 20,000m+ summer drill campaign starting in June.

headline: SEABED NODULE LAND RUSH: NOAA Certifies TMC's USA B License for 1.02-Billion-Tonne Pacific Area
snippet: NOAA formally certified The Metals Company's USA B exploration license application covering 122,000 km² of Pacific seafloor estimated to hold 1.02 billion tonnes of polymetallic nodules rich in nickel, cobalt, copper, and manganese. An Environmental Impact Statement is the next regulatory hurdle; a final license decision is expected before end of Q1 2027.

headline: COPPER AI CRUNCH: One Data Center Needs 27,000 Tonnes — Supply Crisis Deepens at Near-Record $6.40/lb
snippet: AI infrastructure is hammering copper supply chains — a single 1 GW data center requires roughly 27,000 tonnes of copper for wiring and power distribution, and the global buildout is accelerating. China's ban on sulphuric acid exports through December is simultaneously squeezing smelter throughput, with COMEX copper hovering near its May 13 all-time high of $6.71/lb.

headline: RECORD Q1, ROUGH Q2: Gold Miners' Windfall Profits Face 50-100% Fuel Cost Spike from Iran War Oil Shock
snippet: Gold miners posted record Q1 margins with an average realized price near $4,900/oz, but Q2 will see a double squeeze: gold has dropped ~$200/oz from Q1 averages while fuel costs have surged 50-100% in key jurisdictions as the Iran war sends oil prices higher. Remote open-pit operations face 30-40% of their cost structure tied to diesel.

headline: IRAN WAR PREMIUM: Middle East Crisis Is Repricing Uranium From Canada's Athabasca Basin
snippet: The Oregon Group argues the Iran-Strait of Hormuz conflict is embedding an energy security premium into Western utility demand for uranium, reinforcing the bull case for Athabasca Basin producers able to supply without Middle Eastern logistics exposure. Spot uranium holds near $85/lb — down from January's $101 high but still 19% above year-ago levels.

headline: RARE EARTH DEAL IN LIMBO: Rubio Signals New Pressure as US-China Export Licenses Stall Four Weeks After Geneva
snippet: The US-China Geneva agreement to resume rare earth exports reached on May 11 has stalled in implementation — licenses have not been issued and supply chains remain severed. Secretary of State Rubio announced new pressure measures on May 28, and a one-year truce on broader Chinese rare earth restrictions expires in November 2026 with no successor framework in sight.

headline: JOE MAZUMDAR: Q1 Gold Producers — Surging Margins, Declining Output, and Why M&A Is the Only Path to Reserve Growth
snippet: Mining analyst Joe Mazumdar breaks down Q1 2026 earnings across the gold producer universe: margins are exceptional at $4,900/oz average prices, but production is declining as grades fall and no major new deposit has been discovered since 2022. Senior producers have one playbook left — acquire juniors who have already done the hard work.

headline: GOLD-TO-SILVER RATIO MOVING LOWER: Why the Compression Sets Up Explosive Leverage for Silver Stocks
snippet: With gold near $4,463 and silver at $76, the gold-to-silver ratio sits in the low 60s — historically elevated territory that precedes silver outperformance. A ratio compression toward the 40-50 range would imply silver at $90-110/oz at current gold prices, amplifying returns for silver miners with operational leverage to spot.
